title: Machine Learning for the Prediction of Red Blood Cell Transfusion in Patients During or After Liver Transplantation Surgery
summary: Recursive feature elimination and XGBoost selected preoperative predictors for red-cell transfusion during or after liver transplantation. The study reports AUROC 0.813 in a 1,193-patient multicenter cohort and 76.9% accuracy in a separate 31-patient prospective validation; this does not establish patient benefit.
ai_technology: Recursive feature elimination and XGBoost for preoperative transfusion-risk prediction
organization: The Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University; Australian National University; Renji Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

evidence.tested: The model reported AUROC 0.813 in a 1,193-patient, three-hospital cohort and 76.9% accuracy in a separate prospective 31-patient validation cohort.
evidence.unknown: The prospective validation was small; different transfusion criteria, selection and confounding limit interpretation, and clinical benefit was not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Recursive feature elimination selected preoperative predictors and XGBoost estimated red-cell transfusion risk.

source_review.scope: Publisher full-text Methods and Results, including the separate prospective validation cohort; date checked.
